components.text: The Core LLM Agent Paradigm: Building a ReAct Reasoning-Acting Loop From Scratch

components.title: The LLM Decision Dilemma: Static Reasoning vs. Blind Tool Calls
components.analogy:
Background: As academia explored how to improve LLMs' ability to solve complex problems, the field split into two camps: pure Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and pure action (Act-Only).

Core bottleneck: in multi-hop QA benchmarks like HotpotQA, pure CoT can't access up-to-date external knowledge beyond the model's weights, leading to serious hallucination. Pure Act-Only, meanwhile, blindly calls external APIs without global planning or logical reasoning, and easily gets lost in a loop during complex investigation. How can an LLM have both a brain for reasoning and planning, and hands for calling tools?

components.topic: 💬 AI Lab Roundtable: Why CoT and Act-Only Both Break Down on Complex QA

messages.content: Elena, we ran an eval on HotpotQA and found that even with Chain-of-Thought, the model often starts fabricating facts by the second reasoning step in a multi-hop question. What do you think the root cause is?

Because CoT is purely the model reasoning with itself, over its own static parameters. There's no external feedback — once it misremembers a fact mid-way, everything after that is just confidently building on a wrong assumption.
So what if we just plug in a Wikipedia search API directly, and have it skip its own memory and only call tools (Act-Only)?

We tried pure Act mode too — it actually did worse! Once the search returned a wall of text, the model had no explicit thinking step to distill the next search query from it, so it kept re-searching the same term and got stuck in a loop.

So there's a real tension: thinking without acting causes hallucination, and acting without thinking causes blind loops. What if, before every action, we forced the model to first output an explicit trace of its thinking?

That's exactly the closed loop! Have the model first generate a <dfn title="The explicit reasoning and step planning output before an action">Thought</dfn> to plan the move, then output an <dfn title="The concrete instruction the model uses to trigger an external API or tool">Action</dfn> to call an API, and finally feed the resulting <dfn title="The real observation returned by the external environment or API">Observation</dfn> back into the prompt — that way every step can be dynamically corrected against physical facts!

components.title: How ReAct Works: A State Machine Model
components.description: ReAct doesn't change the LLM's underlying neural network weights at all — it uses a prompt protocol to strictly constrain the LLM's output format, physically establishing a control loop that includes reasoning, execution, and environment feedback.
components.diagramTitle: 📊 Tracing the ReAct State Machine Loop
components.diagram:
Input Task ➔ LLM generates Thought (reasoning logic) ➔ LLM outputs Action (extracted tool instruction)
➔ Host environment intercepts the Action and executes the tool ➔ Gets an Observation (environment feedback data)
➔ Observation is appended back into the prompt ➔ Triggers the next Thought ➔ ... ➔ Outputs the Final Answer

pillars.title: Reasoning Trace (Thought)
pillars.description: The model's own thinking and step breakdown before it outputs an action — making complex decisions explainable and dramatically reducing the chance of hallucination.

pillars.title: Action Space (Action)
pillars.description: A strictly formatted tool-call instruction (e.g. Search[query] or Finish[answer]), parsed by regex and executed by the host system.

pillars.title: Observation Space (Observation)
pillars.description: Real data returned by an external tool or environment (e.g. a web page excerpt or an API response), fed back into the model as context for dynamic correction.

components.analogyTitle: 💡 The Core Mental Model, Built From Scratch
components.analogy:
From an implementation standpoint, ReAct is fundamentally just a while(true) loop + a state parser:
1. Prompt protocol: inject few-shot examples telling the model it may only output `Thought:`, `Action:`, or `Final Answer:`;
2. Regex interceptor: when it captures `Action: tool_name[arg]`, pause LLM generation and call a local Python function instead;
3. Context appender: wrap the tool's result as `Observation: ...` and append it to the end of the conversation history, then drive the LLM again.

components.title: The ReAct Synergy Mechanism
components.definition: ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) is a foundational architecture in the agent field. By explicitly defining a Thought / Action / Observation pattern in the prompt, it deeply combines an LLM's internal implicit reasoning ability with the ability to act on the external physical world through tools.
components.example:
// Example of a ReAct-style interleaved trace:
Task: Find the elevation range covered by the eastern sector of the Colorado Plateau
Thought 1: I first need to search for the Colorado Plateau to find the specific geographic areas its Eastern Sector covers.
Action 1: Search[Colorado plateau]
Observation 1: The Colorado Plateau sits in the Four Corners region; its Eastern Sector extends into the San Luis Valley...
Thought 2: The page mentions the San Luis Valley — I need to search for its elevation range next.
Action 2: Search[San Luis Valley elevation]
Observation 2: The San Luis Valley's average elevation is roughly 2,300 to 2,700 meters.
Thought 3: I now have the exact elevation data, so I can give the final answer.
Action 3: Finish[2,300m - 2,700m]

components.title: Architecture Deep Dive: Writing a ReAct Agent Engine From Scratch
components.content:
Building an industrial-grade ReAct agent from scratch doesn't require a heavy framework — at its core it's just a **while loop + a regex-based state parser**:

```python
# Minimal ReAct agent control loop (From Scratch Python pseudocode)
import re

def run_react_agent(prompt_history, tools, max_steps=5):
    for step in range(max_steps):
        # 1. Call the LLM to generate the current thought and action
        response = llm.generate(prompt_history)
        
        # 2. Check whether the Finish termination condition was reached
        if "Action: Finish" in response:
            return extract_answer(response)
            
        # 3. Regex-parse to capture Action: tool_name[arg]
        match = re.search(r"Action:\s*(\w+)\[(.*?)\]", response)
        if match:
            tool_name, tool_arg = match.groups()
            # 4. Execute the locally registered function to get a real Observation
            obs = tools[tool_name](tool_arg)
            # 5. Append the physical feedback, driving the next round
            prompt_history += f"\nObservation: {obs}\n"
```

**Four core infrastructure components:**
1. **<dfn title="A prompt builder containing system instructions and interleaved few-shot format examples">Prompt Synthesizer</dfn>**: injects the format spec, constraining output to a `Thought -> Action -> Observation` structure.
2. **<dfn title="An extractor that uses a regular expression to capture the Action instruction and pull out the tool name and argument">Action Parser & Dispatcher</dfn>**: captures `Action: tool[arg]` and dispatches it to a local Python function.
3. **<dfn title="A context manager that maintains conversation history and appends Observation feedback at the end">Context Accumulator</dfn>**: appends `Observation:` to the end of the conversation history.
4. **<dfn title="A termination-state detector that parses the Finish instruction and breaks the while loop">Loop Termination Gate</dfn>**: breaks the loop and returns the answer once it detects `Action: Finish[answer]`.

questions.question: When building a ReAct engine from scratch, if the Action Parser's regex captures the model output `Action: Search['Python']`, what should the system do at the infrastructure level?
options: A. Print `Search['Python']` verbatim to the terminal and terminate the program
B. Pause LLM text generation, call the local search function to get a result, wrap it as an Observation, and append it back into the context
C. Clear all conversation history and start a brand-new request
D. Let the LLM connect to the physical internet itself
questions.explanation: Once the ReAct engine captures an Action, it pauses LLM generation, calls the corresponding tool in the host environment (Python/JS) to get a return value, then wraps it as `Observation:` and appends it to the context for the LLM's next round of Thought.

components.title: Summary: What ReAct Really Is, and How to Build It
components.analogy:
ReAct isn't a black-box trick — it's a general-purpose control loop that uses a prompt protocol to constrain the LLM's format, and host-side code to intercept Actions and append Observations.
📌 Glossary

In AI agent architecture, the ReAct paradigm solves the static-hallucination problem of traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT). By explicitly separating the Reasoning Trace (Thought) from the Action Space (Action), and appending the Observation feedback after the host environment executes it, ReAct fully transforms an LLM into a dynamic, autonomous system capable of using tools.
